source_title: Mohammed Siraj and Nitish Kumar Reddy set for India A stints ahead of NZ Tests - India Today
source_excerpt:
Mohammed Siraj and Nitish Kumar Reddy will feature for India A in their respective four-day matches against New Zealand A. The move comes as India prepare for the upcoming Test series, while Prasidh Krishna has been ruled out of the ODI leg.
India's preparations for the upcoming Test series against New Zealand are gathering pace, with Mohammed Siraj and Nitish Kumar Reddy set to join the India A squad for their respective four-day matches against New Zealand A. The move will give the duo valuable red-ball game time ahead of the two-Test series, which begins on November 19.
Siraj will link up with India A for the second four-day match, starting October 31, while Nitish will remain with the senior team's ODI squad for the series opener against New Zealand on November 4. The all-rounder will then join India A for the third and final four-day fixture.
There is also a significant development on the fitness front, with Prasidh Krishna likely to return to action in the final India A clash before the Test seires. The pacer, who was ruled out of the five-match ODI series against New Zealand due to a hamstring injury, is expected to join the squad for the final four-day match, subject to clearing his Return to Play assessment.
The India A fixtures will offer the three players an opportunity to build match fitness and rhythm before the Test series. While Siraj and Nitish will get time in the middle, Prasidh's potential return will be closely watched as he works his way back from injury.
India A's updated squad for the second four-day game against New Zealand A: Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sai Sudharsan, Devdutt Padikkal, Yash Rathod, R. Smaran, Dhruv Jurel [C] [WK], Washington Sundar, Mohammed Siraj, Akash Deep, Shikhar Mohan, Mukesh Choudhary, Mukesh Kumar, Manav Suthar, Kumar Kushagra [WK].
India’s updated ODI squad for the first three ODIs: Shubman Gill [C], Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer [VC], KL Rahul [WK], Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Anshul Kamboj, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Ishan Kishan [WK], Mohammed Siraj, Kuldeep Yadav, Nitish Kumar Reddy (only for the first ODI)
India’s updated ODI squad for fourth and fifth ODIs: Shreyas Iyer [C], Rohit Sharma, Virat Kohli, Tilak Varma, Ishan Kishan [WK, VC], Axar Patel, Naman Dhir, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar, Ruturaj Gaikwad, Arshdeep Singh, Kumar Kushagra [WK], Mohammed Siraj, Yash Thakur, Kuldeep Yadav SIRAJ, NITISH TO GET RED-BALL GAME TIME
Siraj's inclusion in the second four-day match will give him an opportunity to build rhythm ahead of the New Zealand Tests. The right-arm pacer has been one of India's key fast-bowling options in the longest format, with 144 wickets in 48 Test appearances.
Nitish, meanwhile, has scored 396 runs and taken eight wickets in 10 Test matches, including a memorable maiden century against Australia at the Melbourne Cricket Ground during the 2024-25 Border-Gavaskar Trophy.
His last Test appearance came against South Africa in the second Test in Guwahati in November 2025. Nitish scored 10 off 21 balls in India's first innings and returned figures of 0/49 with the ball. He will now look to make the most of the India A fixture to get some valuable time in the middle before the New Zealand series.
The 23-year-old has also been in action during India's ongoing white-ball campaign. He played a crucial role in the second T20I against New Zealand in Christchurch, scoring an unbeaten 26 off 13 balls and combining with Tilak Varma in a match-winning partnership. He also picked up a wicket in the game. PRASIDH EYES INDIA A RETURN
Prasidh Krishna's potential return to action is another important development in India's preparations. The pacer sustained a hamstring injury during the ODI series against the West Indies and has since been working towards regaining full fitness.
Although he has been ruled out of the upcoming ODI series against New Zealand, Prasidh is expected to join India A for the third and final four-day match against New Zealand A. His inclusion, however, is subject to clearing the Return to Play assessment.
The fixture could provide Prasidh with the match practice he needs as he builds towards the two-Test series against New Zealand, which begins on November 19. For India, having the fast bowler available again would be a welcome boost to their pace-bowling options. - Ends
